newsitem.title: UK: Crude pipeline to Novorossiisk reopens, port shut.
newsitem.headline: Crude pipeline to Novorossiisk reopens, port shut.

text.p: The crude pipeline feeding Russia's main oil export terminal at Novorossiisk on the Black Sea has reopened on Tuesay after closing on Monday because storage tanks at the port were full, a shipping source said on Tuesday.
"They will be receiving again because they have resumed loadings," the source said.

The 650,000 barrel a day (bpd) port has been closed on and off for bad weather since December 23 but reopened briefly on Monday, allowing two crude tankers, the 60,000-tonne Sea Express II and the 140,000-tonne Matilda, to finish loading.
The port was officially shut again at 2240 (local time) on Monday evening and remained closed early Tuesday but was expected to reopen shortly.
"They will be trying to berth and load this afternoon," the source said.
Six crude tankers were waiting at anchor outside the port.
The port of Odessa was also shut because of high winds. Tuapse was open but the main pipeline to the port was closed for maintenance work, the shipping source said.
Shipping operations at the Baltic port of Ventspils were normal.
